rulings.restated: Input — Do you count this Form 1095-A's column B? Count it unless another Form 1095-A from the same state, whose column B you count, shows coverage in every month this one does. For a month that several forms from one state cover, column B is entered from only one of them; forms from different states, and policies from one state that follow one another, are each counted.
rulings.model: The IRS requires selecting column B 'for that month' and says 'Enter the amount from column B of only one Form 1095-A—do not add the amounts from each form'; a whole-form coverage-containment test counts both forms when their coverage overlaps only partly. It also omits the marriage exception requiring taxpayers to 'add together the amounts from column B of the Forms 1095-A for each month before the first full month of marriage.'
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — the objection is a partial same-state overlap where both forms' column B would be counted and the overlapping months added twice, and the December-2025 marriage with separate plans where column B is added across plans. The project refuses both: f8962.two_counted asks whether two counted Forms 1095-A from one state show coverage in the same month and refuses on yes (i8962 p. 15, Column (b), "Enter the amount from column B of only one Form 1095-A—do not add the amounts from each form."); f8962.marriage refuses a return married in 2025 with coverage before the first full month of marriage, through Part V (i8962 p. 13, Table 4). The render review of this collection form does not include the consuming form's gates.
